quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: ICT & Mobility Solutions FY2026: sales revenue JPY 574,162 million (down 5.4%), core operating income JPY 53.0 billion, down JPY 17.5 billion. Management states display-related materials saw selling prices fall on intensifying price competition, together with the impact of the drastic restructuring of the large LCD polarizing film business; in semiconductor process materials the gradual market recovery continued and shipments increased, but fixed costs rose; a stronger yen reduced export proceeds and the yen value of overseas subsidiaries. Segment production scale about JPY 524 billion (selling-price basis).

quarterly_data.signal: Capital expenditure in FY2026 totalled JPY 121,560 million, mainly new construction, expansion and maintenance of manufacturing facilities, of which ICT & Mobility Solutions JPY 52,970 million. The capex plan for the year after the fiscal year-end is JPY 119,000 million: ICT & Mobility Solutions JPY 41,500 million, Essential & Green Materials JPY 29,500 million, Agro & Life Solutions JPY 18,000 million, Advanced Medical Solutions JPY 10,500 million, Sumitomo Pharma JPY 10,000 million; no significant facility retirements are planned beyond routine renewals. Among major facilities, Sumika Semiconductor Materials Texas (US; semiconductor process chemicals manufacturing) is carried at JPY 35,160 million, of which JPY 27,750 million is tools, fixtures and construction in progress.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Company outlook: for the year ending March 2027 (the company's fiscal 2026) it forecasts core operating income of JPY 215 billion, helped by improved earnings at Sumitomo Pharma and PetroRabigh's financial improvement and shareholding change; from the year ending March 2028 onward, the company aims for the growth drivers Agro & Life Solutions and ICT & Mobility Solutions to lead company results by maximizing the returns on prior investments. Medium-term business plan (fiscal 2025-2027, i.e. the years ending March 2026 to March 2028) targets for its final year, the company's fiscal 2027 (year ending March 2028): core operating income JPY 200 billion, ROE 8%, ROIC 6%, D/E ratio in the 0.8x range; over the medium to long term the company aims to achieve ROE of 10% or more, ROIC of 7% or more and a D/E ratio of about 0.7x.
quarterly_data.figure: year ending March 2027 core operating income forecast JPY 215 billion; medium-term plan target for the year ending March 2028 JPY 200 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: ICT & Mobility Solutions strategy: the company acquired all shares of Asia Union Electronic Chemical Corporation of Taiwan (agreement September 2025, completed January 2026), gaining semiconductor chemical bases in Taiwan and the US. Management states it will put management resources into capturing the growth of the advanced semiconductor market driven by the rapid expansion of AI demand, developing and expanding sales of advanced materials and strengthening stable supply. In displays it restructured the large LCD polarizing film business and is shifting to high-function areas such as OLED and automotive; heat-resistant battery separator production and related functions are being consolidated at SSLM in Korea from the company's fiscal 2026 (year ending March 2027), with Japan concentrating on R&D of next-generation materials.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor R&D (ICT & Mobility Solutions segment R&D JPY 33.4 billion): resources are concentrated on the new markets created by generative AI. Front-end: developing EUV photoresists, building on chemically amplified resists and, for next generations, the company's own organic molecular resist; strategic investment to strengthen immersion ArF resist development and broaden the lineup; high-purity cleaning chemicals with ppt-order impurity control are progressing toward adoption in leading-edge semiconductor processes. Back-end materials (described as at a technology transition): the company is building a track record in thick-film resists for multilayer wiring and cleaners for special processes and aims to expand adoption through a stronger lineup. Also: higher quality large-diameter GaN substrates for next-generation power semiconductors, InP epiwafers for optical communications as data centers spread, ultra-fine alpha alumina (which the company says it was first in the world to mass-produce) for semiconductor polishing, CPU/GPU heat-dissipation materials and chip-equipment parts, and LCP grades for high-speed transmission.
quarterly_data.figure: ICT & Mobility Solutions R&D JPY 33.4 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Petrochemical restructuring: the shareholding in Rabigh Refining and Petrochemical Company (PetroRabigh) was reduced to 15% from October 2025. In December 2025 the company agreed to transfer its domestic polypropylene (PP) and linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) businesses to Prime Polymer, a joint venture of Mitsui Chemicals and Idemitsu Kosan, in two absorption-type company splits (planned to take effect July 1, 2026 and April 1, 2027); Prime Polymer will then be owned 52% by Mitsui Chemicals, 28% by Idemitsu Kosan and 20% by Sumitomo Chemical, and the three companies target annual rationalization of JPY 8 billion or more.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Chemical annual securities report: FY2026 (06-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Advanced medical and regenerative medicine: raguneprocel (brand name Amchepry; allogeneic iPS cell-derived dopaminergic neural progenitor cells, filed in Japan by Sumitomo Pharma in August 2025) received conditional and time-limited approval in Japan in March 2026, which the company describes as the world's first iPS cell-derived regenerative medicine product; a US Phase 1/2 trial continues. The third regenerative and cell medicine manufacturing building, CRAFT, was completed in July 2025; oligonucleotide CDMO production and shipments are in full swing, with a CRO site opened in Marlborough, Massachusetts in April 2025.
